what: Each of the four corners of a work photo card gets a notch piece in the background color. When the card first becomes visible, pieces of its type (no-tr leaves out only the top right and uses three, no-bl leaves out only the bottom left and uses three, diagonal uses two on a diagonal, none uses none) grow around the outer corner as the pivot over .6s cubic-bezier(.6,0,.05,1), carving out the card outline. On hover the pieces shrink away in .4s leaving a full rectangle, and return when the pointer leaves.

options.[data-fx-part=corner]: Home piece (four children) — tl, tr, br, bl via data-key. Missing corners are skipped
options.look: Type, default no-tr — no-tr · no-bl · diagonal · none
options.cycle: Multiple shapes (comma-separated) — with every set, it cycles to the next shape every that many seconds (by default it stays on the first shape)
options.appear: If off, starts already carved in (no growing entrance)
options.hover: With off, hovering does not close the notch (default closes, --fx-hover-dur default .4s)
options.--fx-size · --fx-r: Piece size (share of card width, default 15%), piece inner radius (default 16px) (via style)
options.--fx-notch-bg: Piece color (via style), default --kf-bg — same as the background the card sits on
options.--fx-hover-delay: Interaction response delay (via style), default .09s (original Framer variant delay)
options.--fx-hover-ease: Hover response curve (via style), default --fx-ease — for the Brand variant it is a linear() redrawn from the original

use: …
note: The original builds its shape from the Framer variant Start X → X (bundle’s TL·TR·BR·BL scale 0/1 · .6s [.6,0,.05,1]), and hovering a related work card brings the piece to 0 in 400ms (captured with motion-probe). The big panels in the work strip and work list don’t close the notch on hover, so use hover: off.
